name: Mount Aso: Nakadake and Takadake (阿蘇中岳・高岳)
why: From the green bowl of Kusasenri across the black ash plain of Sunasenri and up the rim of a live volcano, then along the ridge to the 1,592 m top of the Aso caldera.
book: Closed while the eruption alert level of Nakadake is 2 or higher: then nobody may go within about 1 km of the first crater, which takes in Sunasenri and its car park. On 13 November 2026 the level was 2 (since June 2026). Check the JMA bulletin and the Aso visitor centre site the day before: routes open and close with the level.
water: Toilets and drinks at Kusasenri only. No water or shade on the volcano: carry 2 litres.
dangers: Volcanic gas (sulphur dioxide) drifts over Sunasenri and the ridge: leave at once if you cough or smell it, above all with asthma or heart trouble.
A sudden eruption can throw rocks: know where the concrete shelters are.
Loose ash and scree on the crater wall; fog and wind on the open ridge.
Lightning: no cover anywhere on the summit ridge.
turnaround: Gas warning sirens, fog on the crater wall, or not at Nakadake summit by 13:00: go back the way you came.

points.name: Kusasenri
points.note: The grassy crater meadow with its pond, horses and the Aso Volcano Museum. A 45-minute path leads east to the Furubochu trailhead (1,140 m).

points.name: Nakadake crater
points.note: Nakadake summit, 1,506 m, on the rim above the steaming crater, reached up the crater wall from the ash plain of Sunasenri: about 2 hours from Furubochu.

points.name: Takadake summit
points.note: 1,592 m, 25 minutes along the ridge: the highest of Aso's five peaks, with the whole caldera wall around you. Return the same way.
